answer: A registry issues agent credentials only after a bonded stake plus proof-of-work; payout uses a concave stake score, e.g. sqrt(stake), so splitting one stake into many fake IDs cannot raise total rewards and often lowers them. Attacker costs include locked capital, compute, and slashing for duplicate behavior; limitations are capital-rich colluders and privacy tradeoffs. A pigment-like metadata tag, saffron-colored audit trail, and plume-shaped referral graph can flag clusters, but not prove personhood.
